transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, thanks for seeing me. I hope it's okay that I made an appointment for this, I really don't want to waste your time. But, uh... I guess what made me finally ask for help is that I just... I barely want to eat anymore. 

It's probably not a huge deal, but like, I'll be on my lunch break at the store, just staring at food I used to really like, and... I just end up throwing most of it away. I feel really bad about wasting it, I know I shouldn't do that, but I just can't bring myself to eat it. Does that... is that something that makes sense to come in for?
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Um... I don't know if I'd say I'm sad, exactly. I mean, everybody gets a little down sometimes, right? Like, it's just normal to feel a bit off on some days. I definitely don't want to make a big deal out of it or sound like I'm complaining. I guess I've just been feeling a little... flat? But it's not like I'm crying all the time or anything. I hope that's an okay answer. I just don't want to overstate it, you know?
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Um, yeah, I guess... well, like I was saying earlier about not really eating my lunches at the store? Because of that, I think I have lost a little bit of weight. My work pants are definitely fitting a lot looser lately. 

But, um, I don't want to make it sound like I'm wasting away or anything! It's probably not a huge amount, so please don't worry too much about it. It's just... yeah, my appetite is just kind of gone, like I mentioned before. I hope it's okay that I brought that up again. Does that... did that answer your question alright?
Do you feel like you've been enjoying things less often than you used to?

Um, I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want to sound ungrateful for the things I get to do, because I know I'm lucky. But... yeah, things just don't feel the same right now. 

Like, I used to really look forward to going to gallery nights, or, you know, playing basketball with some guys, or just grabbing tacos from a food truck. I even used to help out with this art thing for kids. But lately... I don't know, I just kind of show up and stand there. I feel really bad about it, but I just feel so flat, and I usually end up making some excuse to leave early. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a downer or anything. Is it normal to just kind of lose the spark for stuff like that for a while?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um, well... I guess it's been about two months now? Give or take. 

It kind of started around the time I got this, um, this award for a window display I did at the store. The district manager made a really big deal out of it and gave me all this attention, which was nice of them, obviously! I don't want to sound like I didn't appreciate it. But... yeah, ever since then, I've just been feeling kind of off. 

I hope it doesn't sound silly, letting something like that get to me. Two months isn't that long though, right? I'm sure it'll pass soon. Did that give you the timeline you needed?
Are there any activities that you still enjoy doing?

Um, well, like I was saying before... I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, but I'm struggling to find things I actually enjoy right now. 

I know I mentioned the gallery nights and the basketball, and the food trucks... and even that art program with the kids. I keep trying to go to those things because I know I should, and I don't want to let anyone down. But I really just end up standing there, feeling totally flat, and then I feel guilty so I make up an excuse to go home early. 

I'm sorry, I know I already said all that. I'm trying really hard to snap out of it, I promise. I just... I haven't really found anything else that makes me feel happy right now. Is it okay that I don't have a better answer for you?
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but no longer find pleasure in?

Um, yeah, I think I might have mentioned those earlier? I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I don't want to waste your time. 

But, yeah, it's those same things. The gallery nights, playing basketball with the guys, getting tacos from the food trucks... and helping the kids with their art projects. I really used to get so excited about all of that. I loved it. But now, like I said, I just kind of show up and stand there feeling totally flat. I always end up making some excuse to leave early. 

I feel awful about it, honestly. I don't want to be a flake or let people down. I'm really trying to push through it, you know? I hope it doesn't make me seem lazy or anything. Did I answer that right, or did you mean other stuff besides those?
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

Um, I think... I mean, I really wish I could say yes, because I know I should be doing things and staying active. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around not trying. But... no, not really. 

I keep hoping if I just keep trying different things, something will click, you know? But right now, everything just feels kind of empty. I'm sorry, I know that's basically what I just said a minute ago. I hope it's okay that I don't have a better answer. Am I being helpful at all?
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities that you used to find pleasurable, or is it more that you're just not enjoying them as much as you used to?

Um, well... I guess it's more like I've completely lost interest. I'm so sorry, I know I'm probably sounding like a broken record here, and I really don't want to be difficult. 

But yeah, I used to get so pumped for the gallery nights, or shooting hoops, getting tacos, and especially the art stuff with the kids. I really did love all of that. But now... I just don't care about it anymore. It's not just that it's less fun, it's like the fun is just completely gone. I just stand there feeling totally flat until I can make up a reason to go home. 

I feel terrible about it. I know I should be trying harder to enjoy things, and I really don't want you to think I'm just giving up. I promise I'm trying. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Have you experienced periods of feeling flat or depressed like this before?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days before, like anyone else, you know? But nothing like... nothing like this, where it just drags on and everything feels so empty. 

I really try to keep a positive attitude most of the time, I promise. I'm usually a pretty upbeat guy. I don't want you to think I'm someone who just complains a lot or anything. But yeah, this... this feeling is new for me. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? Is there anything else about my past you need to know?
Have you had more than one period in your life where you felt similarly flat or depressed?

Um, no, definitely not. Like I said, this is all really new to me. I mean, I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. I really have always been the kind of guy who tries to look on the bright side. 

I've never had a stretch like this before in my whole life. I hope that's okay, that this is the first time? I know it probably makes it harder to figure out what's going on, and I'm sorry if that makes your job more difficult. But yeah, just this one time, just lately. Is that alright?
Do you feel like your flat mood and loss of interest are interfering with your daily life at work or with your relationships?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I'm still showing up for my shifts at the store every day, I promise. I really try to be reliable. But... I guess I have been messing up a few things lately. 

Like, my inventory counts have been a little off, and I messed up some of the display plans. My manager has had to double-check my work, which makes me feel awful. I really hate making extra work for him, you know? I'm usually much better at my job, I swear. 

And with my friends and stuff... I guess I have been skipping out on things. Like I mentioned before, the gallery nights and basketball... and I haven't been showing up for the youth art workshops either. I feel terrible letting the kids down. I just... I don't want to be a drag to be around when I'm feeling like this. 

I know I need to do better, and I'm really trying to get back on track. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just slacking off. Does that answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you feel like your flat mood and loss of interest are interfering with your daily life to the point where you're having trouble functioning?

Um, I mean... I wouldn't say I'm completely having trouble functioning, you know? I'm definitely still getting up and going to work every day. I really pride myself on not calling out. 

But... I guess, like I was saying, it is affecting things more than I'd like to admit. The inventory counts being off, and messing up the display plans... my manager having to double-check my work is really embarrassing. I hate being a burden on him. And yeah, skipping the gallery nights, basketball, and... and not going to the youth art workshops. I feel so guilty about the kids. 

So, I guess it is interfering, even though I'm trying really hard not to let it. I just... I don't want you to think I've completely given up or stopped trying. I'm still trying my best. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you feel like your flat mood and loss of interest are severe enough that you're having significant difficulty functioning in your daily life?

Um, oh... I hope I'm not frustrating you, since I know we kind of just went over this. I'm sorry if I'm not explaining it well enough. But, um, no, I wouldn't say it's severe or that I'm having significant difficulty. 

I mean, I'm still keeping my job at the store and taking care of my basic stuff, so I'm not totally falling apart or anything. I promise I'm holding it together for the most part, except for those little slip-ups I mentioned before. I'm really trying my best to stay on top of things and be a good employee. Is... is that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not making it sound worse than it actually is.
Would you say that your flat mood and loss of interest are interfering with your daily life most of the time?

Um, well... I guess I'd have to say yes, most of the time? I'm so sorry, I feel like I keep repeating myself, and I really hope I'm not annoying you. 

Like I said, I'm definitely still showing up for work, so I'm not completely useless or anything. But... yeah, almost every day lately, I feel like I'm dragging. And the mistakes at work—like the inventory counts and the display plans—they've been happening pretty often, which is why my manager has been double-checking my stuff. I feel so bad about that. 

And outside of work, I guess it's been most of the time, too. I've basically stopped going to the gallery nights and basketball entirely. And I'm still skipping the youth art workshops. I just... I don't have the energy, and I feel terrible about it. 

I know I need to snap out of it, and I promise I'm trying. I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right. Is that what you meant by most of the time?
Have your symptoms lasted for more than two weeks?

Um, yeah... it's been more than two weeks. I'd say it's been going on for about two months now? 

I think it really started right after I won that window display award at work, and the district manager started paying so much attention to me. I know I should have been happy about it, and I really am grateful for the recognition, I promise. But... that's kind of when I started feeling this way. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm ungrateful or complaining about doing well at my job. I know two months probably seems like a long time to let this drag on. Am I... am I giving you the right timeline? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Would you say that your flat mood is severe enough to interfere with your ability to concentrate or make decisions?

Um, well... I guess I'd have to say yes, it does interfere a little bit. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I can't do my job at all, because I really am trying my hardest. But, um... yeah, at work I keep losing my place on simple stuff. Like, when I'm counting inventory, I'll just kind of blank out and have to start over. Or when I'm picking colors for a display plan, I just end up second-guessing myself over things I used to do really fast. 

I feel so silly about it, honestly. It's just simple stuff, and I know I should be able to just focus and get it done. I hope my manager isn't too disappointed in me. Does... does that make sense? I'm sorry if I'm making a big deal out of nothing, I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the way you need me to.
Do you feel like your flat mood is severe enough to significantly impact your daily functioning?

Um, well... I guess I'd say it's impacting things a little bit. I don't want to sound like I'm completely falling apart or anything, because I am still going to work every day. I really make sure to show up. 

But, um... yeah, like I mentioned before, I've been messing up the inventory counts and the display plans enough that my manager has had to start double-checking my work. I feel really awful about making extra work for him, I really do. And outside of work, I've just been skipping the gallery nights and basketball entirely. And I haven't been to the youth art workshops I used to help out with, either. 

I know I need to do better and get back on track. I'm really trying not to let it ruin everything. Does that... is that the kind of impact you were asking about? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you feel like your flat mood is severe enough to cause significant distress or impairment in your social or occupational functioning?

Um, I guess it's basically what I was just saying... I really hope it doesn't seem like I'm just whining or trying to get out of things. I mean, I am still going to work every single day, I promise. But, um, yeah... because I keep messing up the inventory and the displays, it's definitely causing some issues there since my manager has to check over everything I do now. I feel so terrible about it. 

And socially, um... I guess it's impaired that, too, since I've completely stopped going to the gallery nights and playing basketball. And I feel really guilty about bailing on the youth art workshops. I know I should be pushing myself harder to go to those things. 

I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself too much. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture. Is that... does that answer your question okay?
Do you feel like your flat mood is severe enough to cause significant distress or impairment in your daily life most of the time?

Um, yeah, I guess it's pretty much all the time now. I really hope I'm not sounding like a broken record, I'm so sorry. I know I just said this, but I am really trying my hardest to keep things normal. I'm still showing up for all my shifts at the store. 

But, um, because I keep getting confused with the inventory and messing up the displays, my manager is having to double-check everything I do. I just feel so bad that I'm making his job harder. And, um, yeah, most of the time outside of work, I'm just not doing the things I should be doing. Like skipping the gallery nights and the basketball games, and not showing up for the youth art workshops. 

I know I need to snap out of it and get back to my regular routine. I really am trying. Does that... I hope that gives you the information you need? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
